title: Nine Minutes and One Chair
subtitle: 预约与约定 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 预约与约定（社会服务与人际沟通·时间与约定）
meta: 主题语境：预约与约定（社会服务与人际沟通·时间与约定）　|　核心词汇：appointment　|　正文 327 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 appointment 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 my mother made ① an appointment for nine o'clock and arrived at eight, and she said the hour was part of the appointment. The ② appointment, meaning the slot and not the doctor, was nine minutes long; an appointment, she said, is the only thing you can be early for and still be late to. She was early nine times and late once, and the once was the one she remembered.

Every ③ appointment she ever kept was written in the same book, in the same hand, and the book was thrown out in 1991. Their ④ appointment with the specialist in the next town had been made in March and happened in September; an appointment, my father said, is a promise made by a stranger about time. He said a stranger's promise about time is the weakest promise there is, and the one people keep best.

My grandmother used the other word and meant the other thing: she had ⑤ an appointment at the school in 1953, which was a job and not a time. The ⑥ appointment, meaning the giving of a job and not the keeping of an hour, is the only kind that changes a life; an appointment, my mother said, is either a job or a wait, and never both.

By 1986 the ⑦ appointment card had been lost twice and the appointment had been moved three times, and she said the moving was the treatment. The  appointment she dreaded was on the ninth of November; an appointment, my father said, is the only thing that gets worse the longer you keep it. She said that was true of promises too.

The  appointment I remember is the one she kept in the rain, for a doctor who had retired in June. An ⑧ appointment, she said in 1990, is the smallest promise two people can make, and the only one that is written down; every appointment, she said, is a way of saying you will still be there.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 预约；约定（一次具体的就诊预约）
B. n. 预约（指那个时间段、那个号）
D. 固定搭配：make an appointment 预约、约定时间
E. n. 任命；委派（一份工作）
F. n. 任命（授予职位这件事）
G. n. 预约（抽象总称）
H. n. 预约（泛指这类约定）

items.q: made an appointment for nine o'clock
The appointment, meaning the slot and not the doctor
an appointment at the school in 1953
The appointment, meaning the giving of a job

answers.why: make an appointment 意为“预约、约定时间”，1984 年母亲约了九点，八点就到了，她说那个钟点也算预约的一部分。
appointment 指“那个时间段、那个号”，预约的时间是九分钟，而不是那位医生。
appointment 泛指“预约这类约定”，她守过的每一次预约都记在同一本册子上。
appointment 意为“一次具体的就诊预约”，他们与邻镇那位专家的预约三月约好，九月才看上。
appointment 意为“任命、委派（一份工作）”，祖母 1953 年在学校的那次“约会”其实是一份工作，不是一个时间。
appointment 意为“任命、授予职位这件事”，与守一个钟点相对，是唯一能改变一生的一种。
appointment 作定语，意为“预约的”，到 1986 年那张预约卡丢了两次，预约改了三次。
appointment 为抽象总称，她说预约是两个人能做出的最小的承诺，也是唯一会被写下来的那种。
